title: AI chip export control moves from silicon to cloud: the neocloud compliance chain
map_limitation: This map cannot see the economics of the private entities that actually run the disputed layer: Megaspeed (the Singapore neocloud ejected from Bridge Data Centers) and Zenlayer (its Los Angeles-based replacement tenant) file nothing public, so the size of the gray-market rental book this whole enforcement mechanism targets is known only through the one $2 billion Nvidia chip purchase Reuters-sourced reporting disclosed, not through a balance sheet. GeoComply, the geolocation-compliance vendor most directly positioned to benefit from the Chip Security Act, is Blackstone/Atairos/Arctos-backed and private, so the chip-location-attestation link's only listed exposure is Nvidia's own R&D spend, already folded into a chip business fully discovered at link one; this map cannot separately price the attestation layer until Nvidia ships it as a product or a rival lists. On the demand side, G42, Core42, Khazna, and Humain, the four named Validated End User entities actually receiving the chips this whole chain exists to gate, are sovereign-linked private companies with no listed equity anywhere; their spending is visible only through the US Commerce Department's own chip-quantity caps (35,000 to 70,000 chips), never through a filing of their own. None of the five public compliance-software names on link four (Descartes, LSEG, Moody's, S&P Global, Thomson Reuters) breaks out export-control or denied-party screening as its own separately reported revenue line, so the impact appraisal's own finding, that this layer's money has not yet found a listed issuer, is directionally right even where an issuer exists: the issuer exists, its revenue contribution from this exact niche does not appear separately anywhere public. The hardware-attestation mandate itself (the Chip Security Act, H.R. 3447 and S. 1705) is pre-enactment, so every ticker on that link's story is a bet on a bill passing, not on a shipped requirement. And this map deliberately excludes a dedicated power and grid equipment link even though Southeast Asian data center buildouts are power-intensive: that link concept is already scored in the ai-infrastructure and data-center-moratoria chains, and repeating it here would be a second expression of a bet already held rather than a new finding (ARCH-005's own instruction).

links.name: Controlled AI accelerators (Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom)
links.role: Nvidia's and AMD's export-controlled AI GPUs (H100/H200/GB200/GB300, MI300/MI308/MI325X) plus Broadcom's custom AI accelerator silicon are the physical item this whole enforcement regime is defined around: every downstream link in this chain exists only to verify where one of these chips ends up and who is actually running it.

evidence.claim: AMD disclosed in an 8-K that a new US export license requirement covering its MI308 AI accelerator, part of the same China/D:5 export control regime this chain maps, was expected to result in charges of up to approximately $800 million in inventory, purchase commitments, and related reserves.
evidence.source_name: AMD 8-K, Item 2.06 (Material Impairments), SEC EDGAR (filed via AMD investor relations)
source_excerpt: a new license requirement implemented by the United States government for the export of certain semiconductor products to China (including Hong Kong and Macau) and D:5 countries
The Export Control applies to the Company's MI308 products.
The Company expects that the Export Control may result in charges of up to approximately $800 million in inventory, purchase commitments and related reserves.

evidence.claim: A BIS final rule effective January 15, 2026 shifted export license review for Nvidia's H200 and AMD's MI325X from presumption of denial to case-by-case for China and Macau, subject to a 25 percent tariff, a 50 percent volume cap, third-party testing, and KYC requirements, while next-generation Blackwell chips remain under presumption of denial.
evidence.source_name: Federal Register, Revision to License Review Policy for Advanced Computing Commodities
source_excerpt: shifting export license review for NVIDIA H200 and AMD MI325X chips to China from presumption of denial to case-by-case evaluation
subject to a 25% tariff, 50% volume cap, third-party testing, and strict KYC requirements

bottleneck.note: Chip supply is real and famously tight, but it is not this chain's distinguishing scarcity, compliant access is. NVDA is the most-covered name in markets and AMD engineered the MI308 specifically to sit under the control threshold and was still caught by it, so this link behaves like ARCH-007 (the semis layer as a leaf in someone else's chain): necessary, already fully discovered, not the candidate.

capture_inputs.notes: Margin has not landed evenly on the two names most exposed to this exact dynamic: AMD's own 8-K disclosed an estimated $800 million inventory and purchase-commitment charge tied specifically to the MI308 license requirement, a direct capture hit from the same control regime this chain maps, while Nvidia's far larger scale let it absorb the same policy uncertainty without a comparable disclosed charge. Not easily routed around: the chip itself is the object being controlled, so substitutability sits with the buyer (which chip to seek), not with the seller.

explainer.what: זה השבב הפיזי עצמו, מעבדי הבינה המלאכותית המתקדמים של אנבידיה ושל היריבות שלה, שכל משטר הפיקוח על הייצוא כולו נבנה סביבו. בלי השבב הזה אין בכלל על מה להתווכח.
explainer.players: אנבידיה ו־AMD הן היצרניות המובילות של השבבים המבוקרים עצמם, וברודקום מייצרת שבבי בינה מלאכותית מותאמים אישית שנופלים תחת אותו הגיון פיקוח.
explainer.why: בלי השבב הזה כל שאר החוליות במפה מיותרות: הן קיימות רק כדי לוודא לאן השבב הזה הגיע ומי בפועל מפעיל אותו.
explainer.bottleneck: זו לא חוליית ההיצע הצר של המפה הזאת, אלא כמעט ההפך: השבב עצמו כבר מוכר ומכוסה עד כאב, והחוליה האמיתית שמגבילה היא הגישה החוקית אליו, לא הייצור שלו.
explainer.hands_to: השבב עצמו עובר הלאה בשתי דרכים מקבילות: אל תוך שכבת אימות המיקום שנבנית סביבו, ואל תוך ידיהם של המפעילים שמשכירים או שמריצים אותו בפועל.

links.name: US export control rulemaking (BIS, Commerce, Congress)
links.role: The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, together with Congress, is the body that decides whether remote or rental access to a controlled chip becomes a regulated act in its own right, and on what timeline: BIS's own guidance, a live enforcement action, and a drafted rule have moved faster than the statute (the Remote Access Security Act) that would give BIS clear authority to write it.

evidence.claim: Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security is drafting a rule that would for the first time target remote access to AI chips rather than their physical movement, blocking Chinese firms from renting Nvidia compute through third-country data centers, with a draft that could reach industry groups as early as September 2026.
evidence.source_name: Forbes, The AI Chip War's New Front: Control The Cloud, Not The Silicon
source_excerpt: The Trump administration's Commerce Department is drafting a new export control rule that would, for the first time, target not the physical movement of chips but remote access to them
a draft could be circulated to industry groups as early as September

evidence.claim: The House passed the Remote Access Security Act 369 to 22 on January 12, 2026, which would give BIS explicit statutory authority to treat remote access to export-controlled items as a regulated act; the Senate companion (S.3519) sat in the Senate Banking Committee for months afterward with no confirmed floor-vote timeline.
evidence.source_name: The Register, Congress votes to close China cloud chip export loophole
source_excerpt: The House of Representatives passed the Remote Access Security Act on Monday by an overwhelming 369-22 bipartisan vote
Passage of the bill through the Senate, and a signature from President Trump, aren't guarantees

evidence.claim: Reporting frames the current draft rule as closing a loophole Commerce itself created when an earlier Biden-era know-your-customer requirement for cloud access to advanced chips was rescinded.
evidence.source_name: Tech Times, Commerce Drafts AI Chip Rule for Loophole It Created by Rescinding Biden Know-Your-Customer
source_excerpt: Commerce Drafts AI Chip Rule for Loophole It Created by Rescinding Biden Know-Your-Customer

bottleneck.note: Nothing downstream has legal teeth until BIS or Congress acts, and multiple export-control law firms have said publicly that BIS may lack the authority to regulate remote access at all until the Senate passes RASA, a bill that sat in committee for months after passing the House 369 to 22. This is the schedule the rest of the chain waits on, ARCH-003's shape exactly: always high impact, always near-zero listed coverage.

explainer.what: זו הרשות האמריקאית שמחליטה אם גישה מרחוק לשבב מבוקר נחשבת בכלל לפעולה שדורשת רישיון ייצוא, ובאיזה קצב היא מגיעה להחלטה כזאת.
explainer.players: משרד המסחר האמריקאי דרך לשכת התעשייה והביטחון שלו, לצד הקונגרס שמנסה להעניק לאותה לשכה סמכות מפורשת בחקיקה.
explainer.why: בלי ההחלטה הרגולטורית הזאת אף חוליה אחרת במפה לא מקבלת שיניים אמיתיות: היא זאת שקובעת אם כל שאר שכבות הציות בכלל חובה מבחינה חוקית.
explainer.bottleneck: זו נקודת צוואר הבקבוק המוחלטת של כל המפה, אבל היא לא סחירה בשום צורה: אין לה מניה, יש לה רק לוח זמנים שכל השאר ממתינים לו.
explainer.hands_to: מהחוליה הזאת יוצא הלחץ הרגולטורי לשלוש חוליות תיווך שונות בבת אחת, שכבת הסינון התוכנתי, הייעוץ המשפטי, ואימות המיקום החומרתי, וגם ישירות אל בעלי מרכזי הנתונים.

links.name: Chip-level location verification and attestation technology
links.role: Cryptographic, latency-based location verification built into the chip itself (Nvidia's own attestation feature) and the legislative push to mandate it industry-wide (the Chip Security Act) are a technology layer distinct from who screens a customer: this is verifying where the silicon physically is, not who is renting it.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported on December 10, 2025 that Nvidia had built a software-based location verification feature, demonstrated privately to customers but not yet released, that uses the confidential computing capabilities already built into its GPUs plus latency to Nvidia-run servers to approximate which country a chip fleet is operating in; Nvidia's own blog post the same day described it as opt-in and read-only, with no hardware kill switch or backdoor.
evidence.source_name: Modern Diplomacy, Nvidia Develops Location-Tracking Tech to Combat AI Chip Smuggling
source_excerpt: Nvidia had developed a software-based location verification feature that would indicate in which country AI accelerators are operating
demonstrated privately to customers
opt-in software for the fleet management of data center GPUs
no hardware tracking technology in the GPUs, no kill switches and no backdoors

evidence.claim: The Chip Security Act (H.R.3447), which would require covered export-controlled AI chips to carry a reliable location-verification mechanism within 180 days of enactment, passed the House Foreign Affairs Committee 42 to 0 on March 26, 2026; a Senate companion (S.1705) was introduced by Senator Tom Cotton.
evidence.source_name: Select Committee on the CCP, House Committee Passes Chip Security Act
source_excerpt: the U.S. House Foreign Affairs Committee voted 42-0
to advance the Chip Security Act, bipartisan legislation to prevent the illicit smuggling of advanced artificial intelligence chips

bottleneck.note: Real and moving, not yet binding. Nvidia's own feature has been demonstrated privately but not shipped, and the Chip Security Act that would mandate location verification industry-wide passed its House committee unanimously but is not law. A genuine chokepoint in waiting, not one yet.

explainer.what: זו שכבת טכנולוגיה נפרדת מהסינון של מי שוכר את השבב: היא בודקת איפה השבב עצמו נמצא פיזית, באמצעות יכולת אימות מובנית בשבב עצמו.
explainer.players: אנבידיה עצמה מפתחת את היכולת הזאת פנימה לתוך השבבים המתקדמים שלה, ולצדה עומדת חברת טכנולוגיית מיקום פרטית שכבר תומכת בחקיקה שתחייב את כל הענף לאמץ יכולת דומה.
explainer.why: בלי יכולת כזאת אין דרך טכנית לאמת שהצהרת המיקום של שוכר תואמת את המציאות, גם אם הוא עבר את כל בדיקות הסינון הפורמליות.
explainer.bottleneck: זו עדיין לא חוליה סגורה: היכולת קיימת בפועל אצל היצרן המוביל אבל טרם שוחררה כמוצר, וההצעה שהייתה הופכת אותה לחובה עדיין לא הפכה לחוק.
explainer.hands_to: כשהיא תבשיל, היא תעבור אל המפעילים עצמם, ספקי הענן העצמאיים וענני הענק המבוקרים כאחד, כתנאי טכני נוסף להפעלה חוקית.

links.name: Denied-party screening and trade compliance software
links.role: Denied-party screening, sanctions-list matching, and trade-compliance data platforms are the software layer every regulated party in this chain, chip maker, neocloud, landlord, or hyperscaler, has to run a transaction through before it can legally proceed, exactly the layer the signal's own retail_gap found no source had named a vendor for.

evidence.claim: Descartes Systems Group reported Q1 fiscal 2027 (quarter ended April 30, 2026) revenues of $193.6 million, up 15 percent year over year from $168.7 million, in a press release furnished to the SEC as Exhibit 99.2 to a Form 6-K.
evidence.source_name: Descartes Systems Group, Form 6-K Exhibit 99.2 (SEC EDGAR)
source_excerpt: Revenues of $193.6 million, up 15% from $168.7 million in the first quarter of fiscal 2026
fiscal 2027 first quarter (Q1FY27)
WATERLOO, Ontario and ATLANTA, Georgia, June 3, 2026

evidence.claim: Descartes' own reporting on the same quarter names Global Trade Intelligence, including sanctioned-party and denied-party screening, tariff and duty content, and foreign-trade-zone tools, as a stated growth driver alongside AI features.
evidence.source_name: Yahoo Finance, The Descartes Systems Group Q1 Earnings Call Highlights
source_excerpt: Global Trade Intelligence and AI were major growth themes, driven by demand for tariff and duty content, sanctioned party screening, foreign-trade zone tools and e-commerce customs processing

evidence.claim: Moody's Analytics, which completed its acquisition of Bureau van Dijk in 2017, integrated an adverse-news, sanctions, and politically-exposed-persons database into Bureau van Dijk's Compliance Catalyst platform, built on the Orbis entity database, extending its KYC and denied-party-style screening capability.
evidence.source_name: Business Wire, Moody's Analytics Strengthens Compliance Platform for KYC Screening
source_excerpt: Moody's Analytics integrated the Grid database of adverse news, sanctions, and politically exposed persons (PEPs) into Bureau van Dijk's Compliance Catalyst platform

bottleneck.note: As close to a hard gate as this map has: a regulated party that fails denied-party screening cannot legally proceed, and the vendor set is a short, named, mostly-public list rather than a diffuse commodity market. Descartes' own most recent quarter shows the category growing double digits.

capture_inputs.notes: Supply is concentrated among a short, named set of platforms (Descartes, LSEG World-Check, Moody's Orbis, S&P Global Panjiva, Thomson Reuters ONESOURCE) rather than a diffuse commodity market, and switching costs are real once a compliance workflow is built around one vendor's case-management and audit trail. Descartes' own most recently filed quarterly results name its Global Trade Intelligence category, which includes denied-party and sanctioned-party screening, as a stated growth driver, evidence that margin is actually landing on this link rather than merely being a pass-through cost center for the operators who use it.

explainer.what: זו שכבת התוכנה שכל גוף מוסדר בשרשרת הזאת חייב להריץ מולה כל עסקה, כדי לוודא שהצד השני אינו רשום ברשימת גופים אסורים או מסונכנים.
explainer.players: קבוצה קטנה של חברות תוכנה ונתונים סחירות מחזיקה בפועל בשוק הזה, ביניהן חברת תוכנת הציות הקנדית, זרוע נתוני הסיכון של בורסת לונדון, וחטיבות ציות של שתי סוכנויות הדירוג הגדולות.
explainer.why: בלי הסינון הזה עסקה פשוט לא יכולה להיחשב חוקית מבחינת רשויות הייצוא, ולכן הוא לא שכבת עלות שולית אלא תנאי סף ממשי לכל שאר הפעילות.
explainer.bottleneck: זו כמעט נקודת הכניסה הכי חדה במפה כולה: מי שנכשל בסינון פשוט לא יכול להמשיך, ורשימת הספקים קצרה ומוכרת ולא שוק סחורה מפוזר.
explainer.hands_to: התוצרת שלה עוברת אל המפעילים בשטח, ספקי הענן העצמאיים וענני הענק כאחד, כתשומה שהם חייבים לרכוש כדי להמשיך לפעול בכלל.

links.name: Export control legal and compliance advisory
links.role: Export-control lawyers and trade-compliance consultancies are the advisory layer that tells every other link in this chain what the rule actually requires and whether a given deal structure survives it, and they are already shaping outcomes: multiple firms have publicly argued BIS lacks statutory authority to police remote access until the Senate passes RASA.

evidence.claim: Export-control counsel have been advising clients on AI-chip-ecosystem risk as the remote-access enforcement theory develops, a body of client-facing legal analysis published by firms including Morrison Foerster, Morgan Lewis, and King & Spalding rather than by any listed company.
evidence.source_name: Morrison Foerster, Managing Export Control Risks in the AI Chip Ecosystem
source_excerpt: Managing Export Control Risks in the AI Chip Ecosystem

evidence.claim: Major US cloud service providers including AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud were reported as concerned specifically about the administrative compliance burden of BIS's drafted remote-access rule, exactly the burden export-control advisory work exists to manage.
evidence.source_name: BigGo Finance, U.S. Moves to Block China's Third-Country Cloud Workaround, Targeting Data Centers in Thailand and Singapore
source_excerpt: major U.S. cloud service providers
administrative compliance burdens

bottleneck.note: A deal genuinely cannot close without this expertise, evidenced by the legal bar actively shaping whether BIS's own draft rule can survive a challenge, but the supply of that expertise is elastic (many competing firms), so it is a real bottleneck without being a chokepoint in the pricing-power sense.

explainer.what: זו שכבת הייעוץ המשפטי שמסבירה לכל שחקן אחר בשרשרת מה החוק דורש בפועל, ואם מבנה עסקה נתון שורד אותו.
explainer.players: משרדי עורכי דין בינלאומיים גדולים שמפרסמים ניתוחים משפטיים שוטפים על כל שינוי רגולטורי בתחום הזה, ולא חברה ציבורית אחת ביניהם.
explainer.why: בלי הייעוץ הזה אף גוף לא יודע אם מבנה העסקה שהוא בונה יעמוד בבדיקה, וזה בדיוק מה שהופך אותו לשכבה שמעצבת בפועל את התוצאה.
explainer.bottleneck: זו חוליה שממשית ומורגשת, אבל לא סגורה כמו שוק תוכנה: יש הרבה משרדים מתחרים, כך שהיא צוואר בקבוק בלי להיות נקודת שליטה יחידה.
explainer.hands_to: הידע המשפטי הזה עובר אל אותם שני מפעילים בשטח, ספקי הענן העצמאיים וענני הענק כאחד, כתנאי מקדים לכל עסקה שהם חותמים.

links.name: Southeast Asian data center colocation landlords
links.role: Data center landlords across Thailand, Malaysia, and Singapore decide, tenant by tenant, who gets to keep occupying the racks: the same physical capacity that hosted the disputed neocloud tenant base is now the capacity being requalified toward an audited hyperscaler tenant base.

evidence.claim: Bain Capital's Bridge Data Centers removed the Singapore neocloud Megaspeed from its Malaysian hub in April 2026 after a US probe into whether Megaspeed, which had purchased nearly two billion dollars of Nvidia chips through a Malaysian subsidiary, had illegally moved advanced AI chips; the roughly 68.4 megawatts of capacity earmarked for Megaspeed was reassigned to Los Angeles-based cloud provider Zenlayer.
evidence.source_name: Bloomberg, Bain Data Center Unit Cuts Ties With Nvidia Buyer After US Probe
source_excerpt: Bain Capital's Bridge Data Centres removed from its Malaysian computing hub Megaspeed International Pte.
replaced it with cloud provider Zenlayer Inc.
Megaspeed International Pte had been allocated 68.4MW of capacity

evidence.claim: Bain Capital was reported in March 2026 to be shopping a stake of up to 70 percent in Bridge Data Centers, whose expansion is financed partly through bank loans that hinge on demonstrating steady cash flow from tenants, precisely the leverage that makes tenant compliance a financing issue and not only a legal one.
evidence.source_name: CNBC, Bain Capital taps buyer interest for Bridge Data Centres, offering up to 70% stake
source_excerpt: Bain Capital taps buyer interest for Bridge Data Centres, offering up to 70% stake
bank loans are a key way for BDC to finance its expansion, which hinge on its ability to demonstrate steady cash flows from tenants

evidence.claim: YTL Power International completed Malaysia's first Nvidia-powered sovereign AI data center in Kulai, Johor in October 2025, a roughly $2.38 billion (RM10 billion) build on Nvidia GB200 NVL72 GPUs, with global hyperscalers named among its customers, the compliant counter-example to the Bridge Data Centers case at the other end of the same Malaysian market.
evidence.source_name: Free Malaysia Today, Malaysia completes first Nvidia-powered data centre in Johor
source_excerpt: YTL Power International Bhd has completed Malaysia's first Nvidia-powered AI data center in Johor
global hyperscalers counting among some of its customers

bottleneck.note: As direct a chokepoint as physical infrastructure gets: Bridge Data Centers simply removed Megaspeed from its Malaysian hub and handed the capacity to Zenlayer instead. The landlord's own financing depends on demonstrating steady tenant cash flow to its lenders, which is exactly the leverage that makes tenant vetting a business necessity, not just a compliance box to check.

capture_inputs.notes: The landlord, not the tenant, holds the switching leverage here: Bridge Data Centers evicted a paying tenant with sunk capacity commitments and replaced it within roughly a quarter, the opposite of a price-taking position. But bank financing dependency (the same Bridge facility carries a large syndicated loan whose lenders were the audience for the memo explaining the switch) caps how much of that leverage becomes pricing power versus simply protecting covenant compliance.

explainer.what: אלה בעלי מרכזי הנתונים הפיזיים במזרח אסיה, מי שמחליט בפועל איזה שוכר ממשיך לתפוס מקום במתקן ואיזה מפונה ממנו.
explainer.players: צד אחד מוחזק בידי קרן השקעות פרטית אמריקאית שכבר פינתה שוכר בעייתי מהמתקן שלה במלזיה, ולצדו עומדים מפעילים ציבוריים סחירים שבנו בעצמם מרכז נתונים מוזן באנבידיה עבור לקוחות ענן גדולים.
explainer.why: בלי הבעלים הפיזי אין למי שמשכיר גישה לשבבים שום מקום להריץ אותם בפועל, כך שהחלטת ההשכרה שלו היא שער ממשי ולא רק פורמלי.
explainer.bottleneck: זו נקודת צוואר בקבוק פיזית ממשית: המקרה המתועד מראה בעל מתקן שמפנה שוכר משלם ומחליף אותו תוך רבעון, וזו בדיוק ההגדרה של שליטה בשער.
explainer.hands_to: ההחלטה של הבעלים עוברת בשני כיוונים נפרדים, אל ספקי הענן העצמאיים שהם עדיין מארחים, ואל ענני הענק המבוקרים שהם מתחילים לארח במקומם.

links.name: Neocloud GPU rental providers
links.role: GPU rental providers, from the private Southeast Asian operators under direct scrutiny to the listed western neocloud sector, are the layer whose entire business model is renting out compute access, and Nvidia's own compliance reviews were reported to be hitting this layer hardest of anyone.

evidence.claim: Neocloud providers, firms whose entire business is renting out AI compute, were described as hit hardest by Nvidia's own customer compliance reviews as they intensified through summer 2026.
evidence.source_name: Forbes, The AI Chip War's New Front: Control The Cloud, Not The Silicon
source_excerpt: Neocloud providers -- the firms whose entire business is renting out AI compute -- hit hardest

evidence.claim: Listed neocloud names were growing rapidly through the same period this compliance mechanism tightened: coverage of the sector's run noted CoreWeave and Nebius both soaring, sufficiently that a new exchange-traded fund was launched to track the group.
evidence.source_name: 24/7 Wall St, CoreWeave & Nebius Are Soaring. This Brand-New ETF Gives Exposure Across Top Neocloud Stocks

bottleneck.note: The layer under the most direct existential pressure in this whole chain: its entire business model, reselling access to controlled chips, is the specific activity the rule under draft would make a regulated act. Reported as hit hardest by Nvidia's own compliance reviews.

notes.text: Archetype review against all seven entries in _archetypes.md before drawing a single link, per the log's own instruction that this is the point of building a fourth-plus chain. ARCH-003 (uninvestable order-book owner) applies cleanly to export-control-rulemaking: BIS and Congress set the schedule every downstream link waits on and neither is a ticker. ARCH-006 (geopolitical counter-response wired in as a first-class link) applies to sovereign-veu-ai-buildouts: the UAE and Saudi Arabia are bystanders to the US-China dispute whose reaction (formalizing Validated End User status rather than risking the gray-market route) is investable in a different place than the event itself, exactly the archetype's own test. ARCH-007 (the semis layer as a leaf in someone else's chain) applies to controlled-ai-accelerators: necessary, already fully discovered, explicitly not the candidate. ARCH-001 (precision manufacturing capacity), ARCH-002 (EPC volume without capture), and ARCH-004 (critical material input) were checked and do not fit: this chain has no manufacturing-capacity chokepoint, no construction/EPC layer, and no physical material input. ARCH-005 (power and grid equipment behind someone else's story) was checked and deliberately NOT applied even though Southeast Asian data centers are genuinely power-intensive: that exact link concept is already scored in ai-infrastructure (power-equipment, that chain's money corner) and data-center-moratoria, and the archetype's own instruction is to check whether a position would be a second expression of a bet already held before scoring it again. No conflict between an archetype and this chain's own shape was found; nothing here overrides the log.

Built entirely from dated WebSearch research this run, no edgar_fts queries queued (a chain build's supplementary discovery motion, not its only one; run universe is where supplier-side EDGAR full-text search does the issuer census). Two evidence items were upgraded to VERIFIED by fetching the underlying SEC filing directly: AMD's own 8-K on the MI308 export-control charge (filed 2025-04-16) and Descartes Systems Group's Form 6-K exhibit carrying its fiscal 2027 first-quarter results (furnished 2026-06-03), both quoted verbatim from the fetched document rather than from a news paraphrase. Every other evidence item is tagged INFERRED per method 4 (a filing citation from an SEC registrant is VERIFIED, dated research is INFERRED otherwise) since it is drawn from news, government press releases, or a company's own non-filing web page rather than a filing. Deliberately kept to 10 links rather than padded toward 15: every link earns its place with a dated, named, checkable fact, including the two zero-ticker links (rulemaking, legal advisory), which are honest findings about where this chain's money is not, not gaps apologized for.

explainer.shape: זו לא שרשרת בקו אחד אלא מפה עם שני שורשים נפרדים שמתלכדים זה בזה. שורש אחד הוא השבב המבוקר עצמו, והשורש השני הוא המנגנון הרגולטורי האמריקאי שקובע אם השכרה מרחוק של אותו שבב נחשבת בכלל לפעולה מבוקרת. שני השורשים האלה מזינים יחד שלוש חוליות תיווך מקבילות, תוכנת סינון לקוחות, ייעוץ משפטי ייצוא, וטכנולוגיית אימות מיקום ברמת השבב, ושלושתן מזינות בתורן שתי חוליות מפעילות: בעלי מרכזי הנתונים במדינה שלישית, ומהם והלאה שני מסלולים נפרדים, ספקי ענן עצמאיים שמשכירים גישה בלי בדיקה מעמיקה, מול ענני הענק האמריקאיים המבוקרים. המסלול של ספקי הענן העצמאיים מצטמצם לכיוון הביקוש הסיני המוגבל שהם עוד יכולים לשרת, ואילו המסלול של ענני הענק מתרחב לכיוון הביקוש הריבוני התואם שהתגבש רק לאחרונה במפרץ, וזו נקודת הביקוש האמיתית של המפה כולה.
explainer.thesis: כל הכיסוי התקשורתי על הסיפור הזה עוצר בשאלה הפוליטית, האם החוק ייסגר ומתי, ואף אחד לא מנסה לענות מי בכלל מקבל תשלום כדי להפעיל את שכבת האימות שהאכיפה הזאת דורשת בפועל. המפה הזו מוצאת תשובה חלקית וממשית: יש קבוצה קטנה וסחירה של חברות תוכנת ציות וסינון גופים אסורים שכבר מדווחות על צמיחה דו ספרתית בדיוק בקטגוריה הזו, וזו לכידת הערך הכי ברורה על המפה כולה. אבל האמת השלמה יותר היא שרוב השחקנים המרכזיים בסיפור, המשכיר שמפנה שוכר בעייתי, הרוכש הסיני שהגישה שלו נחסמת, והרוכש הריבוני שמקבל מעמד מאומת, הם גופים פרטיים לגמרי שלא מותירים כמעט שום עקבה סחירה. וגם שכבת אימות המיקום החומרתית עדיין רק בדרך: הטכנולוגיה קיימת בפועל אצל היצרן המוביל, אבל החוק שהיה הופך אותה לחובה עדיין לא עבר, כך שכל הימור עליה הוא הימור על הצבעה עתידית ולא על דרישה שכבר קיימת.
